degree_class: LM-87 (Servizio sociale e politiche sociali / Social Work and Social Policies). 120 ECTS, 2 years, second-cycle degree. CRITICAL HISTORICAL POINT: this programme was formerly classified LM-50 (Programmazione e gestione dei servizi educativi / Planning and management of educational services) — the MUR/AlmaLaurea transparency record for CODICIONE 0210107305100001 titles the course 'lavoro sociale e politiche sociali - gia innovazione e ricerca per gli interventi socio-assistenziali-educativi (LM-87, ex LM-50)' and lists BOTH classes against the same course code. The reclassification matters far beyond nomenclature: under Italian law (DPR 328/2001) it is the LM-87 class that gives access to the State Examination for Section A of the Albo degli Assistenti Sociali and the protected title of 'assistente sociale specialista' (specialist social worker), which the old LM-50 class did not. For an applicant, LM-87 is therefore the class that makes this degree a professional qualification route rather than only an academic one. [uncertain] — the professional-register consequence is established Italian national law reported by CNOAS and other Italian universities, NOT stated anywhere on unibz's own pages for this programme; and unibz publishes no announcement dating the LM-50 to LM-87 switch.

majors_tracks_study_plans: NO majors, NO tracks, NO alternative study plans and NO dual-study variant — a single 120 CP curriculum for all students, with personalisation delivered through OPTIONAL COURSES (12 CP total: 4 CP in year 1 and 8 CP in year 2) and individual research projects rather than through named tracks: 'It is possible for students to tailor their studies by choosing optional courses and developing individual research projects under the supervision of faculty members.' STRUCTURE per the brochure study plan. YEAR 1 (57 CP): Social Work and Welfare Systems in Transition 12 (Comparative Analysis of Welfare Systems 6 + Social Work Theories, Ethics and Research 6); Research Design and Methodologies 12 (Qualitative Social Research 5 + LAB Qualitative Methods of Social Research 1 + Quantitative Analysis of Social Inequalities 5 + LAB Quantitative Methods in Social Research 1); English for Social Work 1; Sociological Theories of Global Inequalities 6; Innovative Practices in Educational Contexts 5 (4 + LAB Innovative Technologies for the Common Good 1); Transitions and Crises in the Life Course 6; Labour and Social Security Law 6 (5 + LAB Equal Opportunities 1); Internship 5; Optional courses 4. DISCIPLINARY MIX per the brochure: 'sociology, social policy, anthropology, education, psychology, statistics, law, as well as methods of social project design and management of third sector organisations'; flagship themes are sustainable welfare development, social entrepreneurship, border studies, and digitalisation/ethical use of new technologies for marginalised groups. Separately, the brochure prints the 1 CP year-1 law lab as a second line reading 'Labour and Social Security Law' where the course-offering page names it 'Equal Opportunities (lab.)' — apparently a brochure typo. english_only_accessibility: EFFECTIVELY-CLOSED for a candidate who knows only English, but for a DIFFERENT and in one respect harsher reason than the Bachelor in Social Work. (1) ENTRY GATE IS C1 + B2, NOT B2 + B2. Admission requires C1 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language, and failing it means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank: 'the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. A candidate who can certify only English can certify only one language and is excluded outright. The concrete minimum for a Turkish or other international applicant is therefore English at C1 PLUS Italian or German at B2 — a materially higher bar than the bachelor's B2/B2, since a second language must be brought to independent-user level before applying. Language Centre exam registrations for this programme are restricted to C1 and B2 levels only, one level per language per session, so there is no B1 fallback. (2) IN-PERSON INTERVIEW WITH AN EARLY REMOTE-REQUEST DEADLINE. Selection turns on a paper plus an admission interview held in Brixen-Bressanone. The interview itself may be taken in English, German or Italian — a genuine concession — but video conference is available only 'in justified exceptional cases' and the written reasoned request must reach the Faculty Secretariat BY THE APPLICATION DEADLINE, i.e. weeks before the interview and before the applicant knows whether travel is feasible. This is stricter than the bachelor's 7-days-before rule and is the single most easily missed procedural trap for an overseas applicant. (3) TEACHING REALITY IS BETTER THAN THE BACHELOR'S. English carries 29 of 120 CP (24%), including three substantial year-2 courses, versus Italian's 42 CP; German is the minority language at 17 CP. A student with strong English and workable Italian can cover a large majority of the taught credits. (4) EXIT IS C1/C1/B1 — the third-language exit requirement is only B1, one CEFR step easier than the bachelor's B2, and since entry is already C1 in the first language, the graduation delta is: raise the second language B2 to C1, and reach B1 in the third. (5) A NARROW ACADEMIC GATE COMPOUNDS THE LANGUAGE GATE. Entry requires a bachelor in L-39, L-19 or L-40 or, failing that, 18 credits in specified political-science/sociology sectors AND 12 in psychology/education sectors, acquired before the interview — a hard constraint for a foreign applicant whose transcript will not carry Italian SSD labels. (6) EMPIRICAL SIGNAL, AND IT IS MORE POSITIVE THAN THE BACHELOR'S: a non-EU ranking list WAS published for 2026/27 and one non-EU applicant living abroad was admitted (Applicant ID 152237) against the 2-place non-EU quota. Unlike the Bachelor in Social Work, where zero non-EU places were awarded, this programme demonstrably admits international applicants from outside the EU.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato / limited places) with a merit-based ranking list built on a WRITTEN PAPER plus an ADMISSION INTERVIEW, together with a documentary assessment of prior work experience, all preceded by two eliminatory gates: an academic-qualification gate (specified bachelor classes, or 18 + 12 credits in listed SSD sectors acquired before the interview) and a language-eligibility gate (C1 in the 1st AND B2 in the 2nd language). There is NO entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no portfolio, no GMAT/GRE and no undergraduate grade-average threshold. The paper (max 1,000 words) is the only compulsory portal upload: 'In the application portal, you shall: upload the paper.' Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. The Admission Committee is chaired by the Degree Course Director; for 2026/27 the chair in both sessions was Prof. Kolis Summerer, with members Prof. Urban Nothdurfter and Prof. Daniela Salvucci in the Early Bird session, and Prof. Daniele Morselli and Prof. Urban Nothdurfter in the Late session.
academic_requirements: One of four qualifying routes. (1) A BACHELOR IN A LISTED CLASS: L-39 Social Work (D.M. 270/2004); class 6 Social Work (D.M. 509/1999); L-19 Education (D.M. 270/2004); class 18 Education (D.M. 509/1999); L-40 Sociology (D.M. 270/2004). (2) AN EQUIVALENT ITALIAN OLD-SYSTEM QUALIFICATION: Diploma Universitario in Servizio Sociale (DUSS); Diploma Universitario di Educatore Professionale/di Comunità; Diploma di Scuola Diretta a Fini Speciali in Servizio Sociale; Convalida universitaria del diploma di Assistente Sociale under article 5 of D.P.R. 14/1987; Laurea quadriennale in Scienze del Servizio Sociale. (3) AN EQUIVALENT QUALIFICATION GAINED ABROAD. (4) A DEGREE FROM ANOTHER CLASS (or an old Italian degree, or any equivalent degree gained abroad) PLUS a credit portfolio: AT LEAST 18 CREDITS drawn from GSPS-02/A Political science, GSPS-03/A History of political thought, GSPS-03/B History of political institutions, GSPS-05/A General sociology, GSPS-06/A Sociology of culture and communication, GSPS-07/B Sociology of law deviance and social change, GSPS-08/A Economic sociology of work and organisations, GSPS-08/B Urban and environmental sociology; AND AT LEAST 12 CREDITS drawn from PSIC-01/A General psychology, PSIC-02/A Developmental and educational psychology, PSIC-03/A Social psychology, PSIC-03/B Work and organizational psychology, PAED-01/A Theories and science of education and social education, PAED-02/A Methodologies of teaching and special education. TIMING RULE, easy to miss: 'The credit points referred to in point 4 must have been acquired before the interview' — not before enrolment, before the INTERVIEW, which for the Early Bird session means before 19/05/2026. SSD CODES: unibz uses only the POST-2024-REFORM codes here, with no legacy mapping printed. The rough legacy equivalents are GSPS-02/A ~ SPS/04, GSPS-03/A ~ SPS/02, GSPS-03/B ~ SPS/03, GSPS-05/A ~ SPS/07, GSPS-06/A ~ SPS/08, GSPS-07/B ~ SPS/12, GSPS-08/A ~ SPS/09, GSPS-08/B ~ SPS/10, PSIC-01/A ~ M-PSI/01, PSIC-02/A ~ M-PSI/04, PSIC-03/A ~ M-PSI/05, PSIC-03/B ~ M-PSI/06, PAED-01/A ~ M-PED/01, PAED-02/A ~ M-PED/03. FOREIGN DEGREES additionally need a Diploma Supplement showing at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is allowed provided they do not belong to the same class (the document's own example is 'LM-87/LM-87') and differ in at least 2/3 of course contents. entry_exam_or_test: NONE in the sense of a written admission test — no unibz admission exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT/GRE and no subject test. The selective instruments are a WRITTEN PAPER (max 1,000 words) and an ADMISSION INTERVIEW, scored together out of 80 points. The only formal EXAMINATIONS connected with admission are LANGUAGE exams at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants who choose that route of proof. Dates for 2026/27: Early Bird — online, 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late — online, 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). No Language Centre exam session exists for the Additional Application Session, and the additional-session page states plainly that 'the unibz Language Centre does not offer language exams for this application session', so an applicant in that window must already hold accepted external proof. LEVEL RESTRICTION: for this programme 'you can only register for C1 and B2 level exams and only for one level per language' — the example given is that one may register for a C1 German and a B2 Italian exam in the same session, but not a C1 and a B2 German exam. Separately, AFTER admission there is a non-selective THIRD-LANGUAGE PLACEMENT TEST for admitted students who cannot certify their third language; the date is communicated by e-mail and the result assigns a learning path aimed at reaching B1.
selection_scoring: The admission procedure is based on two criteria totalling 100 points. (1) PAPER/MOTIVATION LETTER AND ADMISSION INTERVIEW — MAX 80 POINTS IN TOTAL, assessed jointly. The paper of no more than 1,000 words must make clear: 'why you want to enrol for the degree', 'the skills and knowledge you have that will be relevant for studying this subject', and 'your expectations'. The interview 'aims to develop the topics presented in the paper previously and to explore your motivation and skills'. (2) WORK EXPERIENCE GAINED WORKING IN THE SOCIAL OR EDUCATIONAL FIELDS — MAX 20 POINTS. Tie-break: 'In the event of equal scores, the younger applicant will have priority.' NO minimum passing score is published — unlike Design (42/100), Critical Creative Practices (60/100), EMMA (55/95) or Entrepreneurship (70/100) — and there is no undergraduate grade-average requirement, no Webometrics bonus and no OFA-triggering threshold. 'The Admission Committee will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline.' NOTE ON STRUCTURE: unlike the Bachelor in Social Work, where the motivation letter is a separate unscored criterion and the interview alone carries 80 points, here the paper and the interview are explicitly bundled into a single 80-point assessment — so the written paper does carry scoring weight, though its share of the 80 is not published. COMPETITION SIGNAL for 2026/27: demand ran slightly below capacity but the programme is far closer to full than the Bachelor in Social Work. Early Bird admitted 10 EU/equivalent against 15 EU Early Bird places, and 1 non-EU against 2 non-EU places; Late admitted 8 EU against 5 Late places plus 5 Early Bird carry-over places (10 available). Cumulative EU admissions 18 against the 20-place EU quota, leaving roughly 2 EU places for the Additional Application Session. The binding constraints are therefore the C1/B2 language gate, the academic-credit gate and the interview logistics — not the score. [uncertain] — the split of the 80 points between the paper and the interview is not published; no minimum passing score is published; no documentary standard is given for the up-to-20-point work experience; and both 2026/27 ranking decrees publish only rank positions and Applicant IDs with NO scores, so no empirical cut-off can be derived.
bonus_points: NONE. There is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Entrepreneurship and Innovation) and no extracurricular-activity bonus. The only credit for anything beyond the paper and interview is criterion 2 of the ordinary rubric — up to 20 points for work experience gained in the social or educational fields, which is part of the 100-point scale rather than a bonus added on top of it. Those 20 points are nonetheless a genuine structural advantage for career-changers and practitioners: the brochure states the programme 'is designed for both recent bachelor graduates with no previous work experience and professionals already working in the field who wish to further their studies', which confirms the experience criterion is meant to be discriminating rather than decorative. The only other preference mechanism is the age tie-break in favour of the younger candidate. No published definition exists of what counts as qualifying work experience (paid employment, internship, civil service, volunteering) or how it must be evidenced, since the portal upload list names only the paper.
portfolio_and_materials: NO portfolio, NO video, NO project proposal, NO reference letters and NO CV are formally required — the only substantive material is the PAPER / MOTIVATION LETTER, capped at 1,000 WORDS (note: a WORD limit, unlike the Bachelor in Social Work's 6,000-CHARACTER limit). Its required content is prescribed: why you want to enrol for the degree; the skills and knowledge you have that will be relevant for studying this subject; your expectations. The admission-information document's portal instruction list contains exactly one item: 'In the application portal, you shall: upload the paper.' The paper is not merely an eligibility document — it is scored jointly with the interview inside the 80-point band, and the interview is built on it ('The interview aims to develop the topics presented in the paper previously'), so it functions as the agenda for the oral assessment. No file format or file-size limit is published for it (contrast the 20 MB PDF portfolio cap of the design/creative programmes). No language is prescribed; since the interview may be held in English, German or Italian and unibz generally accepts documentation in any of the three teaching languages, the paper is presumably acceptable in any of the three. Candidates must upload the required documents by the application deadline; once submitted the application cannot be modified, and 'filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration'. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. [uncertain] — the permitted language(s) and file format of the paper, and the documentary evidence required to claim the 20 work-experience points, are not specified in any published unibz document for this programme.
interview: YES — the admission interview, taken together with the paper, is the CENTRAL selection instrument and carries up to 80 of the 100 points. Published dates for 2026/27, one per application session: EARLY BIRD — 19/05/2026; LATE APPLICATION — 21/07/2026; ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION — 16/09/2026. (Note the additional-session interview is 16/09, five days later than the Bachelor in Social Work's 11/09, even though the two programmes share the same application window.) PURPOSE: 'The interview aims to develop the topics presented in the paper previously and to explore your motivation and skills' — so it is a defence of the submitted paper, not a general-knowledge or current-affairs test (which is what the bachelor's interview is). LOCATION: in person in Brixen-Bressanone; exact location and time are published on the study programme website. LANGUAGE: 'You can choose whether to attend the admission interview in English, German or Italian' — decisive for international applicants, because the selection conversation need not be in Italian or German. REMOTE OPTION, AND ITS TRAP: 'In justified exceptional cases, the interview can be organised via video conference. In this case, you must provide at least by the application deadline a written and reasoned request to the Faculty Secretariat.' Two things make this harder than the bachelor's equivalent: the standard is 'justified exceptional cases' rather than 'serious logistical difficulties', and the request must be filed BY THE APPLICATION DEADLINE (e.g. 28/04/2026 for Early Bird) rather than 7 days before the interview. An overseas applicant must therefore decide on and request remote participation at the moment of applying, roughly three weeks before the interview date. Faculty Secretariat contact for that request: faculty.education@unibz.it, +39 0472 014000.
conditional_admission: Applicants who have not yet graduated may apply and are admitted CONDITIONALLY: 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application: you can apply, but you will be admitted conditionally and you need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' The enrolment deadline for all three 2026/27 sessions is 13/10/2026 at noon. This is a widely used route in practice — in the Early Bird ranking list 4 of the 10 admitted EU applicants are flagged with an asterisk as not yet holding the degree at application (Applicant IDs 153911, 109929, 152478, 151745), and 1 of the 8 in the Late list (109867). CONSEQUENCE OF MISSING IT: 'If you graduate after the enrolment deadline: you cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list.' unibz gives an explicit financial warning attached to this: 'In this case you should not pay the tuition fees to secure your admission.' LATE-ENROLMENT SAFETY NET: 'You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there still are available places, you can enrol by 11 December 2026' — i.e. 2026-12-11, and only if the request is approved and places remain. SEPARATE CONDITIONAL TRACK for route-4 applicants: the 18 + 12 SSD credits must be acquired BEFORE THE INTERVIEW, so that requirement cannot be deferred to enrolment the way the diploma can. Holders of a foreign qualification are additionally admitted 'with reserve' until the recognition documents are uploaded — the ranking decrees state 'Fino a quando non avrai caricato la documentazione sopra indicata, potrai essere ammesso/ammessa solo con riserva'; if the qualification is judged suitable the reserve is lifted, otherwise the applicant is excluded, and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. Non-EU applicants living abroad are admitted with a further reserve, lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. NOTE: the 120/140 ECTS conditional-admission thresholds used by some other unibz masters (e.g. Data Analytics) do NOT appear for this programme — unibz sets no partial-credit threshold here, only the diploma-by-enrolment rule.
ofa_rules: NONE. No OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) exists for this programme: neither the admission-information document nor the programme page contains an OFA section, a mathematics or other diagnostic test, or grade thresholds that would trigger additional learning requirements. OFA is in any case primarily a bachelor-level instrument at unibz (Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics, Tourism Sport and Event Management use test-based OFA). At master level the functional equivalents here are two, and both are genuine constraints: (1) the ACADEMIC one — route-4 applicants must have acquired 18 credits in the listed political-science/sociology sectors and 12 in the listed psychology/education sectors BEFORE the interview, a prerequisite that must be satisfied up front rather than remedied afterwards; and (2) the LINGUISTIC one — an admitted student who cannot certify the third language must sit a placement test, is assigned a learning path, and needs B1 in the third language from the second semester of year 1 in order to sit curricular examinations held in that language.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the language rule is ELIMINATORY: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' ENTRY: 1st language C1, 2nd language B2, 3rd language no level required. FROM THE 2ND SEMESTER OF YEAR 1: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that language. EXIT (to graduate): 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B1. Language positions are defined by the applicant's own proficiency, not by which language it is: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. Because the admission levels are C1 and B2, applicants may register at the unibz Language Centre for C1 AND B2 EXAMS ONLY, one level per language per session. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language take a placement test (details by e-mail) and are assigned a learning path 'so that you will be able to reach level B1 as soon as possible'. Language Centre courses are FREE: extensive courses 4 hours per week during semesters, intensive courses 6 hours per day between semesters, and a three-week pre-semester intensive session 01-18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day). A1 beginner courses are offered ONLY in that September pre-semester session and 'will no longer be offered during the academic year', so absolute beginners must start there — a trap for anyone admitted through the Additional Application Session, whose ranking list is only published by 18/09/2026, after the intensive courses have ended, and who is warned to acquire A1 independently beforehand. Stated target: the free courses 'aim to help the students reach the level B1 in the third language after the first study year'. Documentary note: a final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: C1 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required. This 'C1/B2/none' pattern is the HIGHER-TIER unibz trilingual entry profile: the same as Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance and Master in Accounting and Finance, and one CEFR step harder in the first language than the Bachelor in Social Work (B2/B2/none) or the Bachelor in Computer Science. Position is set by the candidate's own strength ranking, not by which language it is, so any combination of German, Italian and English at C1 + B2 satisfies the rule — for a typical international applicant this means English C1 plus Italian or German B2. The direct operational consequence is that the unibz Language Centre accepts registrations only for C1 and B2 level exams for this programme, one level per language per session; there is no B1 route and no possibility of being admitted on remaining places with a weaker second language. A second distinguishing feature: from the second semester of year 1 a B1 in the third language becomes a hard prerequisite for sitting exams delivered in that language, and because the curriculum spreads compulsory credits across all three languages in both years (year 1: Italian 25 CP, English 12 CP, German 11 CP; year 2: Italian 17 CP, English 17 CP, German 6 CP), that threshold binds in practice rather than in theory — a student whose third language is Italian would be blocked from roughly 25 CP of year-1 exams without B1.
exit_levels: To graduate: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B1 (CEFR). Compared with the Bachelor in Social Work (C1/C1/B2 exit), the third-language requirement is one CEFR step EASIER here. The graduation delta from the entry profile is therefore relatively contained: a student admitted at C1/B2/none must raise the SECOND language from B2 to C1 and go from zero (or A1) to B1 in the third language within two years — versus the bachelor student, who must raise two languages to C1 and reach B2 in a third over three years. Free Language Centre courses are structured to support exactly this, with the stated aim that students 'reach the level B1 in the third language after the first study year', and A1 beginner courses available only in the September pre-semester intensive session. The 1 CP compulsory course 'English for Social Work' in year 1 signals that English academic literacy is treated as a taught competence rather than assumed.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is required FROM THE 2ND SEMESTER OF THE FIRST YEAR as the minimum level for taking the curricular examinations held in that specific language: 'a B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language'. This is a binding rather than nominal constraint here, because compulsory credits are spread across all three languages from the first semester. A student whose third language is ITALIAN would be blocked from roughly 25 CP of year-1 exams and 17 CP of year-2 exams — the largest exposure, since Italian is the dominant language at 42 CP overall. A student whose third language is GERMAN faces the smallest exposure, 11 CP in year 1 and 6 CP in year 2 (German is the minority language at 17 CP overall), which makes German the least costly choice of third language on this programme — the reverse of the situation on the Bachelor in Social Work, where German is compulsory and heavy from semester 1. A student whose third language is ENGLISH would be blocked from 12 CP in year 1 and 17 CP in year 2. Note that B1 is also the EXIT level for the third language on this programme, so clearing this semester-2 threshold effectively discharges the graduation requirement as well — unlike the bachelor, where B1 is only an interim step toward a B2 exit. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test and are assigned a learning path targeting B1. There is no programme-specific mid-January deadline of the kind imposed by the Bachelor in Computer Science.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways. (1) THE MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF THE FINAL HIGH-SCHOOL YEAR, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian); for foreign qualifications, 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your hign school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction' (typo in the original). (2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE TAUGHT IN ITALIAN, GERMAN OR ENGLISH — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if it is not on the degree. This route is especially relevant at master level, since every applicant by definition holds a bachelor degree — an applicant whose bachelor was taught in English is recognised at C1 in English, which alone satisfies the 1st-language requirement. (3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) LANGUAGE EXAMS ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, registered online in the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application. ONLINE exam dates for 2026/27: Early Bird 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). C1 AND B2 LEVELS ONLY for this programme, one level per language per session; 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' No Language Centre exam session exists for the Additional Application Session. ADDITIONAL ROUTE for foreign and bi-/multilingual schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English are explicitly stated on the graduation diploma and all four skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2ND AND/OR 3RD LANGUAGE (not the 1st), subject to Language Centre approval; the school-leaving certificate is uploaded under the respective language in the 'upload language certificates' section. Administrative detail: a final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'), a trilingual DE/IT/EN document applying university-wide. Rules, verified directly in the PDF: (1) the certificate must 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself'; (2) it must show adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer; (3) 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the exam was passed' — the LOWEST sub-skill governs; (4) 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation'; (5) 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list' — the list flags the exceptions with an asterisk reading 'Also accepted as "home edition"'; (6) certificates covering single skills issued by different organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational institutions, and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers, lectors or teachers are not recognised; (9) 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January.' Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf

If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' scholarships_grants: NO programme-specific scholarship exists for this degree — the only routes are the general unibz/provincial ones. MAIN ROUTE: the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, administered by the Office for Higher Education Support (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario) in three annual categories — ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants fostering postgraduate studies. Applications are filled in and sent through the provincial e-government service online, with assistance available from the South Tyrolean Students Association (sh.asus). Grant holders also receive a refund of the tuition fees paid for the academic year, and foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship are exempt from tuition fees outright. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is therefore effectively ineligible in year one, which on a two-year master means half the degree is unfunded by this route. Other listed sources: Italian government grants, Austrian and German (BAföG) grants, DAAD summer-course scholarships, and loans from Italian banks. Contact: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign university degree must upload the bachelor degree diploma, an official translation into Italian (not required for documents issued in German or English), and the DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT showing 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme' — the master-specific requirement, absent at bachelor level. Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein — a Statement of Correspondence of the bachelor degree, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA; (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. Until that documentation is uploaded the applicant is admitted only 'con riserva' (with reserve); 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents', and a candidate found not to possess a valid admission qualification 'can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/ . Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses; the application is filed at the Faculty Secretariat, and the Faculty organises appointments for the preliminary evaluation of previous university careers (in Italian and in German). A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT RECOGNITION QUESTION arises here that does not arise for most masters: because LM-87 is the access class for Section A of the Italian professional register of social workers, an applicant holding a social-work qualification obtained outside the EU who wishes to practise in Italy must additionally go through the professional-title recognition procedure via the Italian Ministry of Justice, which is entirely separate from CIMEA/ARDI academic recognition. non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only, 02/03-28/04/2026 (€50 non-refundable fee) → file any video-conference interview request by that same 28/04/2026 deadline → be available for the admission interview on 19/05/2026 in Brixen-Bressanone → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (2 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/). The Universitaly application is MANDATORY — 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol', and the ranking decree is blunter: 'La mancata preiscrizione su Universitaly comporta la nullità della domanda di preiscrizione e di immatricolazione presentata all'università' (failure to pre-enrol on Universitaly voids the application and enrolment submitted to the university). Only ONE study programme may be selected on Universitaly. The Italian diplomatic authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa; unibz warns that admission does not guarantee a visa or even an appointment at the Italian consular representation, and that holding a study visa confers no automatic right to complete enrolment. NON-EU ADMISSION IS PROVISIONAL IN AN EXTRA WAY: per the ranking decree, non-EU applicants living abroad are admitted with reserve, and 'la riserva viene sciolta previa comunicazione ufficiale, inviata direttamente all'unibz, dal consolato italiano all'estero' — the reserve is lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. FINANCIAL MEANS for the visa: at least €800 per month for living costs, excluding tuition fees; unibz states that 'a master programme will cost € 24,000' in total over the two years combining tuition and living expenses; health insurance and visa expenses on top. AFTER ARRIVAL: the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be applied for within 8 WORKING DAYS of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities are entitled to a refund. uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF and brochure both carry 'Latest update: 28.07.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change'. Verified 2026-08-29. TIME-CRITICAL: the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 are closed and their ranking lists are published, but the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (18/08-04/09/2026, EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only) is OPEN at the verification date and closes at noon on 04/09/2026 — six days later — with the admission interview on 16/09/2026 in Brixen-Bressanone and no Language Centre exams available in that window. (1) PROGRAMME IDENTITY AND HISTORY. The single most consequential finding in this record is that the course is the renamed and RECLASSIFIED successor of the LM-50 'Innovazione e Ricerca per gli Interventi socio-assistenziali-educativi' / 'Master in Innovation and Research in Social Work and Education Sciences', active in Bressanone since 2010. Evidence: the MUR/AlmaLaurea transparency record titles CODICIONE 0210107305100001 as 'lavoro sociale e politiche sociali - gia innovazione e ricerca per gli interventi socio-assistenziali-educativi (LM-87, ex LM-50)' and lists both classes; and the legacy URL slug /master-innovation-research-social-work-and-education/ still resolves to the current page. However, NO unibz document dates the reclassification or the renaming — secondary summaries place the LM-50 period at roughly 2010-2019, but this could not be confirmed, and the year of the change is therefore unresolved. (2) DEGREE-CLASS CONSEQUENCE NOT STATED BY UNIBZ. The claim that LM-87 gives access to the Italian State Examination for Section A of the Albo degli Assistenti Sociali and the title 'assistente sociale specialista' rests on Italian national law (DPR 328/2001) as reported by CNOAS and other Italian universities. unibz's own English pages for this programme never mention the professional register, the State Examination, or the profession of social worker at all — they describe only generic 'management, coordinating and advisory positions'. This silence is itself notable and means the professional pathway should be verified with the Faculty before an applicant relies on it. (3) TEACHING-LANGUAGE WEIGHTING is reconstructed by cross-referencing the per-course language tags on the unibz course-offering page for 2026/27 ('Enrolled from 2025' plan) with the year allocation in the brochure study plan; unibz publishes no per-language credit summary. Optional courses (12 CP), internships (10 CP) and the thesis (10 CP) carry no fixed language and are excluded from the per-language totals. Unlike the Bachelor in Social Work, the full two-year plan IS tagged, so the whole-degree share is computable. (4) CREDIT-VALUE CONFLICT BETWEEN OFFICIAL SOURCES. The unibz study-plan web page disagrees with the brochure and the course-offering page on at least five credit values (Criminal and Restorative Justice 10 vs 6; Ethnography 5 vs 6; year-1 internship 4 vs 5; year-2 internship 8 vs 5; year-2 optional courses 10 vs 8) and asserts 60 + 60 CP where the brochure sums to 57 + 63. This record follows the brochure/course-offering pair, which agree with each other; the discrepancy is unresolved and the study-plan page may simply render its table poorly to automated extraction. The brochure additionally appears to mis-label the 1 CP year-1 law lab, printing 'Labour and Social Security Law' where the course-offering page names it 'Equal Opportunities (lab.)'. (5) SCORING GAPS: the paper and the interview are scored jointly out of 80 with no published split between them; no minimum passing score is published; no documentary standard is given for the up-to-20-point work experience; and both 2026/27 decrees publish only rank positions and Applicant IDs, with no scores and no list of excluded applicants, so no admission cut-off and no count of language- or credit-based exclusions can be derived. (6) The ranking PDFs print 'Bressanone, data della firma' / 'Brixen, Datum der Unterzeichnung' instead of a typed date, so signature dates are unrecoverable. (7) MISSING 'COURSES WILL BE STARTING' BANNER. Unlike the Bachelor in Social Work, this programme's page carries no explicit start-confirmation banner. The programme is nonetheless clearly running (published signed ranking decrees; listed as 'Application possible' in the additional session), but the usual confirmatory sentence cannot be quoted. (8) COHORT SIZE IS VERY SMALL. The AlmaLaurea transparency record shows 1 graduate in 2025, 4 in 2024, 5 in 2022 and 13 in 2020; satisfaction data is suppressed for 2025 because the sample (1 respondent) is below the 5-unit threshold. These figures describe earlier curricula and tiny cohorts, so they indicate scale, not current quality. Admissions for 2026/27 (18 EU + 1 non-EU) are considerably larger than recent graduate counts, which may reflect the recent restructuring, attrition, or both. (9) SCHOLARSHIPS: the unibz study-grants page names the three provincial grant categories but publishes no amounts or merit thresholds; the commonly cited €1,680-€6,960 range and 27/30 merit average could not be confirmed on any unibz page verified for this record. There is no programme-specific scholarship. (10) FEES CONFLICT: one secondary source quotes €1,347.50 per year; all current unibz sources state ca. €1,200 per year (2 x €600). The unibz figure is used here. (11) OFFICIAL CALL: no manifesto or Rector's decree opening the 2026/27 procedure was located at a public English URL, and no LM-87-specific admission/study regulation could be inspected. (12) TURKISH-APPLICANT RELEVANCE: Türkiye's status as a Lisbon Convention signatory (hence case (b) recognition: ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification) is inferred from convention membership, not stated by unibz for this programme. The two decisive practical traps for a Turkish applicant are (a) the C1 + B2 two-language entry gate, which cannot be met with English alone, and (b) the requirement to file any video-conference interview request BY THE APPLICATION DEADLINE rather than shortly before the interview. (13) No 'study career' Excel template, no OFA, and no partial-ECTS conditional-admission threshold apply to this programme. (14) A 2027/28 online info session is likely (one was held on 20 March 2025 for the 2025/26 cycle) but is not currently announced.
